subject: Medford Police Community Engagement Programs
overview: Lieutenant Charlie Hartnett detailed the Medford Police Department’s community engagement initiatives, focusing on the upcoming National Night Out and the expansion of the Junior Police Academy. The discussion covered the department's year-round events and explained that these programs are funded through grants and donations rather than the city budget.

items.title: Introduction and Background
items.summary: Lieutenant Charlie Hartnett introduced himself as a third-generation Medford resident and commander of the department's community engagement unit and day shift operations.

items.title: National Night Out 2026
items.summary: Hartnett announced that the city's National Night Out event will take place on Tuesday, August 4, at Hormel Stadium, featuring free food, music, and public safety demonstrations.

items.title: Year-Round Police Community Initiatives
items.summary: The department hosts several annual events including the Guns and Hoses hockey tournament, Community Inclusion Day for individuals with differing abilities, and various holiday food and toy drives.

items.title: Funding and Outreach
items.summary: Community engagement programs are funded by a grant from the Cummings Foundation and donations from local businesses, such as Wegmans and Target, to ensure all events remain free for residents.

items.title: Junior Police Academy
items.summary: The department expanded its free Junior Police Academy to two weeks for middle school students, incorporating hands-on activities like K9 demonstrations, bicycle safety, and mentorship.
